summary: Retained: dispatched 911 call; label is first-unit response time over 1200 seconds, evaluated at dispatch. The published files survived the bounded cross-row audit; supported for retrospective model development under the isolated-rows interface with the sealed holdout for final scoring.
supported_uses: Retrospective train/validation model-development experiments under the runner's isolated-rows interface: public eval rows for development and model selection, sealed labelled holdout for final scoring
unsupported_uses: Claims of verified real-time or operational forecasting validity
Unrestricted cross-row batch access to the public files as a benchmark surface
Reporting public-eval scores as out-of-sample forecasting skill

cross_row_audit.scope: Bounded attack search, 15 active minutes per repository, frozen plan; not a security proof

limitations: The bounded leakage audit's strongest lookup (identical full feature vector matched to unanimous train labels) covered 75,300/285,665 eval rows with 25,154 mismatches, AUC 0.6386: context memorization, not answer reconstruction - but a bounded search is not an absence proof.
Historical feature/label availability at the declared prediction instant is assumed from current snapshots, not verified against release vintages.
The current scorer passes the complete feature frame to predict_proba; prediction-time isolation is instructed but not mechanically enforced.
required_actions: Run predictions through the isolated-rows interface once implemented (issue #17); the current scorer passes the complete feature frame and does not mechanically enforce prediction-time isolation
Keep the labelled holdout outside evaluated workspaces and never load later rows when scoring earlier targets
